issues.output:
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: included type is not a record type
 --> i1646.bal:7:27
  |
7 | type WithAlias record {| *Alias; boolean flag; |};
  |                           ^^^^^

ballerina: compilation contains errors
issues.edge_case_reason: Record inclusion through a type alias of a record rather than the record name itself.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: valid program rejected with SEMANTIC_ERROR 'included type is not a record type' (no BIR). Spec 5.4.2: inclusion 'includes fields from a named record type'; Alias names the type described by Plain's record-type-descriptor, so it should compile and print '5 true'. Clean-context check: ambiguous under a strictly literal reading but leans valid. No duplicate found (related: #1289, #1295).

issues.title: [Bug]: object field is in scope without self in a method body
issues.edge_case_reason: Ordinary class method referencing a field name (common mistake that must be diagnosed).
issues.reasoning: Reproduces: compiles and main panics 'unexpected'. BIR for get() emits '%0 = n; return;' (bare n, return value never set) — missing diagnostic, so frontend. Spec 6.8.1: fields are not implicitly in scope in a method body; expected 'undefined symbol n' at line 4. Clean-context check confirms. Related but different: #1296, #1562.

issues.title: [Bug]: module init can call a function that reads a module variable before it is assigned
issues.edge_case_reason: Definite assignment of a no-init module variable across a call from the module init function.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces: compiles, prints 0 then 5. Spec 8.7: module-no-init-var must be definitely assigned at each reference; show() reads value before init assigns it. Spec does not pin the error location across calls (clean-context check: medium-high confidence the program must be rejected). Missing diagnostic → frontend. Related: #972 (same rule, direct reads in init; open, could serve as parent), #1636.

issues.title: [Bug]: module variable initializer can read a module variable before init assigns it
issues.edge_case_reason: A module variable initializer reading a module-no-init variable that is only assigned in init.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces: compiles, prints 51 (other computed from zero value). Spec 8.7 + module initialization order (initializers run before init) → compile error expected at line 4. Missing diagnostic → frontend. Clean-context check confirms. Related: #972 (possible parent), #1637, #1282, #1483.

issues.title: [Bug]: re-narrowing after an in-loop assignment hides the assignment to a variable narrowed outside the loop (unsound)
issues.edge_case_reason: Variable narrowed outside a loop, reassigned in the loop body, then re-narrowed by a type test with an abrupt branch.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces: compiles, prints 1 then s (an int-typed y holds a string — unsound). Spec 7.12 forbids an in-loop assignment to a variable narrowed outside the loop when the block can complete normally afterward. Missing diagnostic in the type checker → frontend. Clean-context check confirms. Regression gap of closed #992.

issues.title: [Bug]: member access evaluates the key expression before the container expression
issues.edge_case_reason: Observable only when both the container and key expressions have side effects.
issues.reasoning: Reproduces: prints key before container. Dumped BIR calls key() (bb0) before container() (bb1), so the BIR is wrong for the source → frontend (BIR gen, indexBasedAccess). Spec member-access-expr: container is evaluated before key. Clean-context check confirms. Related but different: #1217.

issues.title: [Bug]: xml:elements / xml:elementChildren panic "invalid XML element name filter" when the name matches no element
issues.output:
error: invalid XML element name filter
        at main(i1633.bal:5)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces: panics 'invalid XML element name filter' at line 5. lang.xml elements/elementChildren are pure filters by expanded name; a name that matches no element should yield an empty sequence (expected 0,0,0,<a/>). Lang library behaviour → langlib. Clean-context check confirms. No duplicate found.
